name: Benson 1996
question: Does abdominal sacral suspension with paravaginal repair yield better outcomes than vaginal sacrospinous suspension with paravaginal repair for significant pelvic support defects?

design.blinding: not reported; postoperative examination by a nonsurgeon coauthor

arms.label: Abdominal colposacral suspension with paravaginal repair
vaginal bilateral sacrospinous vault suspension with paravaginal repair

design.population: Eighty-eight women had cervical prolapse to or beyond the hymen, or vaginal vault inversion exceeding half its length with anterior wall descent to or beyond the hymen.
design.description: Prospective randomized abdominal versus vaginal surgical comparison

verdictNote: Optimal effectiveness favored abdominal repair; the abstract gives no prespecified testing threshold.
takeaway: In women with significant pelvic support defects, abdominal colposacral suspension plus paravaginal repair had higher optimal effectiveness than vaginal bilateral sacrospinous suspension plus paravaginal repair (58% versus 29%) at a mean 2.5 years among 80 evaluated women.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Benson JT, Lucente V, McClellan E. "Vaginal versus abdominal reconstructive surgery for the treatment of pelvic support defects: a prospective randomized study with long-term outcome evaluation." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1996;175(6):1418-1422. doi:10.1016/s0002-9378(96)70084-4
reports.followUp: 1–5.5 years among 80 evaluated women; mean 2.5 years

results.measure: Asymptomatic, apex above levator plate, and no vaginal tissue beyond hymen
results.note: Reported relative risk is for abdominal versus vaginal repair. The abstract does not state a prespecified primary endpoint or testing threshold; numerators are not supplied.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Study Design and Results

results.measure: Symptomatic, apex descent greater than half its length, or vaginal wall beyond hymen; reported with reoperation
results.note: Reported relative risk is for vaginal versus abdominal repair. The abstract does not supply event numerators.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Study Design and Results

harms.label: Urinary tract infection and incontinence
harms.note: The abstract gives no event counts or comparison estimates for either outcome.

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent incontinence
harms.note: Percentages are reported without event counts or explicit denominators for this subset; they cannot be reconciled exactly with the evaluated-arm sizes.

harms.label: Other reported morbidity
harms.note: The abstract groups overall morbidity, complications, hemoglobin change, dyspareunia, pain, and hospital stay without absolute values.

delivery.label: Procedures and follow-up examination
delivery.value: Vaginal bilateral sacrospinous vault suspension and paravaginal repair versus abdominal colposacral suspension and paravaginal repair; ancillary procedures as indicated. A nonsurgeon coauthor examined women standing at maximum strain yearly for up to 5 years.

delivery.label: Catheter use, operative time, and hospital charge

values.exp: Shorter catheter use; longer operating time; higher charge
values.ctl: Longer catheter use; shorter operating time; lower charge

delivery.note: Only direction, not absolute values, is reported in the abstract.
